title: Tight bounds for positive discrepancy via eigenvalues
summary: Given an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix $M$ with largest eigenvalue $λ_1\geq 0$, it is easy to show that the solution of the optimisation problem $\max_{v\in [-1,1]^n}v^TMv$ is at most $λ_1 n$. We prove the following converse: if every $n'\times n'$ principal submatrix of $M$ has maximal eigenvalue at least $λ$, then $\max_{v\in [-1,1]^n}v^TMv\geq λ(n-n'+1)$. This allows us to lift results about the second largest and the smallest eigenvalue of graphs to the (a priori more difficult) setting of positive discrepancy and MaxCut.
